Instructions for BST260 projects, 2026

Vincent Carey

2026-11-09

Source: vignettes/instructions.qmd

Objectives

  • use knowledge and tools encountered in BST260 to
    • extract interesting information in public datasets of interest
    • document uncertainties and paths forward in data interpretation
  • use R’s pkgdown capabilities to produce GitHub pages documenting your work

Tasks to begin

Infrastructure, accomplish by Nov 16 2026

  • fork this repository “https://github.com/vjcitn/bst260project-template” into your account
  • rename the repository to “finalproject” – it should be a public repository
  • use the GitHub IDE “Settings” for the repository to enable “Pages” and use the main branch and /docs folder for page management

Proposals, accomplish by Nov 18 2026

  • Edit the document vignettes/proposal.qmd to state your plans regarding the project
  • Address your proposal to the “BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026”
  • Use the requirements noted below to guide the writing of your proposal

Requirements

  • you must produce a valid R package and pkgdown site that can be seen at github.com
  • you must write at least two vignettes addressing analysis tasks with two different datasets encountered in the class, or approved by instructor if you are introducing new data
  • you must provide
    • full documentation of data provenance
    • descriptive statistics on the variables of interest
    • clear statement of investigative objectives
    • scientific report of findings and limitations

Example datasets

  • The NHANES or NHANESraw data from the NHANES package
  • The CDC data on waterborne illnesses discussed in class here under “Exploring the US CDC API”. The data are accessible via
data(waterborne, package="bst260project") # once package is installed
  • The CDC data on gun homicides that we explored in problem set 3. The data are accessible via
data(cdcmurd, package="bst260project")
  • The RAND corporation data on firearms legislation in the USA. The data are accessible via
data(gunleg, package="bst260project")
